what_its_for: Ganciclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat or prevent a viral infection called CMV (cytomegalovirus). This infection can be serious in people with weakened immune systems, such as those who have had an organ transplant or have HIV/AIDS. The eye gel form (Zirgan) is used to treat a CMV eye infection called CMV retinitis and certain herpes eye infections.
how_to_take: Ganciclovir comes as a capsule to swallow by mouth, as an injection given by a healthcare provider through a vein (IV), and as an eye gel. Take the capsules with food to help your body absorb the medicine and to reduce stomach upset. Do not crush, chew, or break the capsules. For the eye gel, wash your hands before use, tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid gently, and place one small drop of gel inside your lower eyelid. Try not to touch your eye or eyelid with the tip of the tube. Blink a few times after applying. If you wear contact lenses, ask your doctor before using the eye gel.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your weight, kidney function, the type of infection being treated, and whether you are treating or preventing CMV. Take the exact dose your doctor prescribed at the times they tell you. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Your doctor may do regular blood tests to check your dose and make sure the medicine is safe for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for advice.
storage: Store capsules at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep them in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Store eye gel at room temperature and throw it away 60 days after opening. Keep all forms of this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet or pour them down a drain unless told to do so. Ask your pharmacist how to safely throw away medicines you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child while taking ganciclovir, as it can cause birth defects or harm an unborn baby. Women should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping. Men should use condoms during treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid contact with the capsule powder if the capsule is broken, as it can be harmful to your skin and eyes. Ganciclovir can weaken your immune system, so try to avoid being around people who are sick or have infections. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or have blurry vision. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: unusual bruising or bleeding, signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat, extreme tiredness or weakness, decreased urination or swelling in your legs or ankles, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, confusion, shaking, or seizures, sudden changes in your vision, severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting, skin rash or allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. These could be signs of serious side effects that need medical attention right away.
when_it_works: Ganciclovir starts working against the virus soon after you begin treatment, but it may take several days to weeks before you notice your symptoms improving. It is very important to keep taking the medicine exactly as prescribed, even if you feel better, because stopping too early can allow the virus to come back or become harder to treat. Your doctor may check your progress with regular blood tests or eye exams.
special_populations: Older adults and people with kidney problems may need a lower dose because ganciclovir is removed from the body through the kidneys. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. This medicine is not recommended for use during pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk. It should not be used while breastfeeding. Children may use ganciclovir, but the dose will be carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's weight and condition. People with low blood cell counts (such as low white blood cells or platelets) should be closely monitored because ganciclovir can lower blood cell counts further.
